correctness.rationale: For the six-vertex fully bidirected complete bipartite graph the directed arc vertex-set has cardinality 18. Face condition is indegree and outdegree at most one at each graph vertex and no directed cycles; a separate weak-component test characterizes the same disjoint directed paths. Exhausting all 2^18 bitmasks yields 714 nonempty faces with vector (18,108,264,252,72), independently recomputed. The source finite certificate and inspected verify.py give exactly 336 face-poset matching pairs with a complete directed Hasse topological sort over 714 vertices/2376 incidences: one critical 0-cell, five degree-2, 24 degree-3, twelve degree-4 cells. Signed integral cancellations at unit pivots preserve the cellular chain type; the resulting D3 is 5x24 with explicit determinant +1 on columns indexed 6304,33952,35088,65676,67716, while D4 (24x12) vanishes. The five primitive relations kill the five 2-spheres in the Morse CW 2-skeleton; 19 degree-3 generators remain. For a wedge of 19 S3, pi3=H3=Z^19, so zero D4 implies the twelve 4-cell attaching maps are all null; the full homotopy splitting follows. Separate independent GF2 boundary ranks (17,91,173,60) yield (1,0,0,19,12) as a corroboration, not proof of attaching maps.
residual_risks: The homotopy conclusion uses low-dimensional CW attaching-degree classification after exact integral Morse cancellations; modular Betti numbers alone do not imply it.
The statement is for fully bidirected K3,3 only; one-way chessboard complexes are different.

value.rationale: The first balanced nontrivial complete bipartite bidirected digraph has a naturally defined path-selection complex whose integral homotopy is not captured by known one-way chessboard models. Its explicit mixed-dimensional wedge, including 19 lower-degree spheres beyond the twelve top Hamiltonian classes, resolves a meaningful finite low-dimensional boundary and supplies a reusable exact benchmark without pretending to classify all K_m,n.
residual_risks: The graph-specific calculation is not a parameter-family theorem; it remains valuable as a complete natural case with an integral attaching-map certificate.

limitations: No family-wide recurrence or equivariant refinement is claimed; homotopy relies on legal integer cancellations and CW attaching classification.
